name: Hip and buttock padding

card.summary: Foam or fabric padding worn under clothes to add fullness at the hips and buttocks, raising the apparent hip-to-waist ratio for a curvier silhouette.
card.aka: hip pads, butt pads, padded underwear, padded shapewear
card.note: Effect lasts only while worn; pre-made versions are sometimes described as looking lumpy.

quick.overview:
Hip and buttock padding adds volume at the hips and rear so that the waist looks smaller by comparison. Padding is worn under clothing and gives a curvier shape immediately, without surgery.

The idea is old: padded rolls, crinolines and bustles reshaped the silhouette in earlier centuries, and today cis and trans women, drag performers and cosplayers use pads.
quick.how: Homemade pads are usually cut from high-density polyurethane foam and worn inside a compression garment that lifts and shapes the buttocks. Ready-made padded underwear has pockets for removable inserts, and made-to-measure garments are built from the wearer's measurements.
quick.risks: The effect lasts only while the padding is worn. Pre-made garments are criticised by some users for looking lumpy or artificial. Compression garments worn tightly can be uncomfortable.

lead: Hip and buttock padding is a clothing accessory that increases the apparent size of the hips and buttocks, raising the apparent waist-hip ratio and giving a curvier silhouette.[1]
It is used by cis and trans women who want fuller curves, cross-dressers, drag performers and cosplayers. Drag queens use it to create round hips, sometimes exaggerated for comic effect.[1]
The practice has historical precedent: padded rolls widened the hips in sixteenth and seventeenth century Europe, followed by crinolines and hoop skirts in the 1800s and bustles from 1868.[1]

angle.text: The padding adds visible volume where the wearer wants it, immediately and without surgery. The look lasts while the garment is worn.

paras: Homemade padding is usually cut from upholstery-grade foam and worn in a compression garment. Ready-made options are padded underwear with pockets for removable inserts, and custom garments are made from the wearer's measurements and cost more.[1]

Bum rolls appeared in 1500s and 1600s Europe, then hoop skirts and crinolines, and bustles from 1868 added back volume.[1] Twentieth-century transfeminine periodicals such as Transvestia recommended hip pads.[1]
Most contestants in a 2022 season of RuPaul's Drag Race UK vs. the World used foam padding, according to the encyclopedia account.[1]

No studies found on cosmetic hip padding. Separate research on medical hip protectors for older adults, which are foam or plastic pads worn to reduce fracture risk after falls, is a different product category.[2]
